Subject: Dedicated nodes: preemption during scheduled maintenance (impacting tail latency)

Jordan —

Quick background: last week we saw three short windows during which a subset of our dedicated pool in us-west was preempted for host maintenance. Each event lasted ~10–12 minutes while nodes were migrated; we saw a 200–350ms spike in 99.9th-percentile token latency for a small percentage of requests. Our platform SLO is 99.9 availability for inference requests (app-level), and these transient spikes pushed us close to the edge for feature traffic.

We understand some host-level maintenance is unavoidable, but we need clarity on how Redwood will treat dedicated capacity preemption so we can map this to our incident runbooks and contractual SLOs. Specifically we need answers to: 
- What advance notice do you provide for scheduled host maintenance that may cause dedicated node preemption?
- Is there an option to keep a small standby set (warmed KV caches / preloaded models) so we don't get tail-latency spikes during migrations?
- If a maintenance event is unannounced or causes measurable latency degradation, what commercial remedy / credits do you propose?
- Can traffic be diverted automatically to cross-region failover or a compatible hosted variant during short migrations?

We're in a renewal conversation (deal id DEAL-4821) and procurement/legal want a clear operational amendment for our Dedicated terms that covers preemption behavior and remedies. Can we set up a call this week?

Thanks,
Helen Torres
Director, Platform Operations
Stellar Bank

Hi Helen —

Thanks for the note and for flagging this. Im sorry you hit those spikes — we try to avoid customer-visible preemptions in Dedicated pools but, as you note, host maintenance on underlying cloud infra can cause short node moves.

High level proposal (we can review on a call):
- Notice window: provide 72-hour advance notice for planned maintenance that will require draining Dedicated nodes. For cloud-initiated critical maintenance well aim for 48h where feasible and notify as soon as we have visibility.
- Standby warm pool: offer an opt-in standby set for committed Dedicated customers (kept warm with preloaded model weights and KV cache where possible). Activating standby for a migration should cut tail spikes to negligible levels; there will be a small incremental monthly charge for reserved standby capacity.
- Short-notice remediation: for unannounced preemptions that cause a measurable tail-latency degradation (defined below), propose a commercial remediation: 3% of monthly committed spend credited for each distinct incident that exceeds the threshold (capped at 15% per month) during the first 12 months after amendment.
- Routing: automatic temporary routing to compatible hosted model variants is possible; latency and regulatory concerns (data residency) will determine eligibility.

Next steps: Ive looped in Tessa (legal) and I want to pull laura_bennett from SRE to validate feasibility and define the detection criteria for a "measurable tail-latency degradation". Are you available Thu 10/15 or Fri 10/16 for a 30m sync?

Jordan Blake

Team —

Technical constraints and suggested engineering language below. High level: we can practically deliver strong protections but a hard 72h requirement for all cloud-initiated maintenance is brittle across some providers. Recommendation is to adopt a bounded policy that combines notice windows, standby warm pools, and deterministic spillover behavior.

Feasibility notes: 
- Underlying reality: Dedicated pools map to cloud instances that occasionally require host maintenance that can force live migrations. Many clouds provide a 48–72h tentative window for planned maintenance, but they can issue expedited actions in rare emergency cases (weve seen <0.5% of maintenance events be emergency).
- Standby warm pool: we can support this by reserving a small percentage of the customer's committed capacity (configurable 2–10%). Warm pool startup time depends on model size and quantization—typical warm time range: 30s to 5m.
- Detection: we can implement the proposed signal: compute rolling delta on per-customer 99.9th token latency with a baseline window and trigger when delta >100ms for >5m AND >=1% traffic affected. We must ensure sampling/aggregation windows are consistent to avoid false positives.
- Spillover routing: we can route to a compatible hosted model variant automatically if: (a) customer opts in, (b) traffic meets residency/compliance rules, and (c) routed variant cost/latency is acceptable. Routing will be limited to capacity available in region and may incur usage charges.

Operational amendment suggested edits (engineering-friendly):
- Change "72-hour notice" to "72-hour target notice for planned maintenance; 48-hour target when we have tentative scheduling; exceptions may apply in confirmed emergency maintenance events."
- Add: "Standby Warm Pool: Redwood will offer an opt-in standby warm pool sized to the Customer's profile (2–10% typical). Standby warm pools will be provisioned with preloaded model weights and warmed KV caches when possible; expected warm-up latency depends on model and quantization profile and will be documented per-customer."
- Add telemetry & reporting clause: "Redwood will provide per-incident telemetry including: start/end times, affected node IDs, 99.9th-token-latency baseline and incident windows, percent of traffic affected, and remediation actions taken. Reports will be available in the Console and as scheduled exports (CSV)."
- Commercial remedy refinement: propose adjusting to 3% credited per qualifying incident, but for enterprise negotiations be prepared to move to 5% for repeat incidents within a 90-day rolling window. Cap at 15% per month remains reasonable.

Implementation work: I will raise RED-5821 to track the warm-pool orchestration, detection plumbing, and Console reporting. ETA: 8 weeks for the detection and reporting plumbing, 12 weeks for warm-pool orchestration in a limited rollout.

If Sales wants to offer the 90-day trial, engineering can support the pilot with monitoring and a post-trial report. Recommend final position for the customer call: 48h/72h target notice language + opt-in standby warm pool + 3% incident credit (with escalation to 5% if repeat within 90 days) + detailed telemetry.

—Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
